title: #43 Catherine S. Neal: Taking Down the Lion

reader_summary.headline: I'm your host, Eri Parmion, and with me here in the studio is my friend and colleague, Niklas Savos.
reader_summary.overview: I'm your host, Eri Parmion, and with me here in the studio is my friend and colleague, Niklas Savos. I've really been looking forward to our upcoming interview since I love to read about corporate scandals and I was not disappointed by reading this book. In today's episode of Investing by the Books, we have the great pleasure of speaking to Katherine Esnil.

key_points.text: Kathy has worked as an attorney and is since 2005 an associate professor of Business Ethics and Business Law at Northern Kentucky University.

key_points.text: She's also the author of Taking Down the Lion, which we will discuss today.

key_points.text: The book covers the story of the big American conglomerate, Tyco International, and its long-time CEO, Dennis Koslovsky.

key_points.text: In 2001, revenues amounted to 36 billion dollars, and Business Week ranked Tyco the number one performing company in the S&P 500.

thesis: The book covers the story of Tyco International and its CEO Dennis Kozlowski, detailing how the company grew from a small firm to a massive conglomerate before Kozlowski was convicted of grand larceny and other crimes for wrongfully taking $100 million from the company. The author highlights unique aspects of this case, noting that Tyco never declared bankruptcy despite the scandal, its financial statements were not materially restated, and the criminal charges were brought by a local district attorney rather than the federal government.
